objective: Prove: (1) subdividing every triangle of K_m into j^2 gives K_{jm} (j = 2, 3); a refinement step is all-or-nothing in every order, because a split edge forces both its triangles to split; it maps a tube to a tube, so it keeps the seed's shape and never places a corner; (2) in ring accretion around a corner (each ring vertex completed to degree 6, or a convex turn made a corner), making the four turns of ring m corners gives exactly K_m, and K_m arises only that way; (3) with each turn decided on its own, ring accretion also closes into non-round two-kind spheres (exhaustive enumeration and random coins); (4) in single-strip accretion a turn's radius-w decision window is the same in every lap, so a label-free rule decides the four equator turns alike only by chance; one bit kept for one lap makes it exact, but that bit is history the process supplies, a hidden witness under the canonical test; (5) the window law of one order, run in random orders, closes only small round spheres or sticks. Check by computation with controls.
status: Proved 2026-11-07: refinement (subdividing every triangle) maps K_m to K_jm, is all-or-nothing in every order and keeps the seed's shape, so it never places a corner; ring accretion gives K_m exactly when the four turns of one ring become corners, and with turns decided one at a time it also closes lopsided spheres (38 distinct closures up to 100 triangles, 3 round; 12 of 400 random-coin runs non-round, up to 646 triangles); in single-strip accretion a turn's decision window is the same in every lap (w <= 5), so tying the four corners needs a carried bit, a hidden witness under the canonical test.
title: Refinement shares its coin, accretion must carry it
